newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: U.S. Triton-Vuko wins 94.5 pct of Kazakh oil firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Triton-Vuko wins 94.5 pct of Kazakh oil firm.

text.p: The head of Kazakhstan's new state-owned oil company, Kazakh Oil, said on Wednesday Triton-Vuko Energy Group Ltd of the U.S. had won a tender for a 94.5 percent stake in the republic's Karazhanbasmunay oil enterprise.

"They (Triton) have won the tender for the Karazhanbas oil field," Kazakh Oil chief Nurlan Balgimbayev told a news conference in the Kazakh capital Almaty. "There are just a few details that need to be finalised."

Balgimbayev gave no further details of the deal and a senior official at the former Soviet republic's State Committee for Privatisation underlined that Triton and the Kazakh government still had "to meet to work out some remaining questions".
The ailing Karazhanbasmunay enterprise operates several oil fields, including the Karazhanbas field, in western Kazakhstan's Mangistau region on the Caspian Sea.
Oil industry sources in Almaty say working fields contain around 85 million tonnes of crude and estimated further reserves of around 225 million tonnes.
The sources add that production at the enterprise has fallen from around 1.2 million tonnes in 1991 to just 680,000 tonnes in 1996.
